q: Should office and canteen emissions be included in a product carbon footprint?
title: Office overheads in a product footprint
short: A product footprint usually covers the processes that make the product. Office lighting, canteens and staff travel are often left out as non-attributable under the GHG Protocol Product Standard, if you say so. In a company inventory they always count. Keep the two figures separate and state the boundary.
audience: Manufacturers preparing product footprints for buyers

ul: Include: process fuel, electricity, materials, packaging, inbound transport.
Often excluded: offices, canteens, R&D, business travel.
State every exclusion in the report.

p: Allocate site overheads by production share, such as tonnes or machine hours, and show it as a separate line.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.

sources.label: GHG Protocol standards, including the Product Standard
